title: Tracked move deletions are included in the final Word text

evidence.quote: Tracked changes are resolved to the document's *final* state
resolves tracked changes to the final document state (w:ins kept, w:del dropped)

reasoning: Word represents tracked moves with w:moveFrom for the old location and w:moveTo for the new location. The adapter promises final-state parsing and skips w:del/w:delText, but all other containers recurse, so w:moveFrom text is retained instead of being treated like deleted text. Documents with pending tracked moves will show duplicated or stale text in DocGit diffs.
reproduction: Create a docx paragraph containing <w:moveFrom><w:r><w:t>old place</w:t></w:r></w:moveFrom><w:moveTo><w:r><w:t>new place</w:t></w:r></w:moveTo>. parseDocx currently includes both strings; final-state text should include only the moveTo content.
recommendation: Treat w:moveFrom and w:moveFromRangeStart/w:moveFromRangeEnd subtrees as deleted content, while continuing to recurse into w:moveTo like w:ins.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tracked-change test only covers w:del and w:ins, so the default recursion path for w:moveFrom is never exercised.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a parseDocx test with w:moveFrom and w:moveTo in one paragraph and assert only the moved-to text remains.
minimumFixScope: Update collectRunText in the Word adapter and add a focused tracked-move fixture.
